Welcome. These pages hold **everything** you need for *Animal Tracking in
Conservation Biology*: slides, R exercises, datasets and further reading.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Everything here is public and permanent. Slides open in your browser — press
`F` for fullscreen, `S` for speaker notes, `E` for print/PDF view, `?` for all
shortcuts. Exercises are plain web pages you can work through at your own pace.
:::

## What this course is about

Biologging has changed what we can ask about animals. A collar that reports a
position every hour produces more raw observations in a week than a generation
of field naturalists could collect in a career. The bottleneck is no longer
data — it is **asking a well-posed question and knowing which analysis answers
it**.

Over eight two-hour meetings we go from *how do you put a tag on an animal* to
*how do you infer, from its trajectory, what the animal was doing and which
parts of the landscape it chose*. Every concept is paired with code you run
yourself, because tracking analysis is a craft you learn by doing.

## The five themes

::: {.class-card}
[Theme 1]{.topic-badge}

### Movement and movement analysis
Why animals move, the movement-ecology framework, and the full toolbox for
tracking them — from toe-clipping to Argos satellites. Then the quantitative
description of a trajectory: steps, turning angles, speeds, home ranges.

→ [Class 1](classes/class-01/slides.qmd) · [Class 4](classes/class-04/slides.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Theme 2]{.topic-badge}

### Informatics tools: GIS in R
Coordinate reference systems, vector and raster data, and the `sf` / `terra`
stack. Then the specifics of tracking data: Movebank, `move2`, `amt`, cleaning
duplicates and outliers, and making a map you would not be ashamed to publish.

→ [Class 2](classes/class-02/slides.qmd) · [Class 3](classes/class-03/slides.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Theme 3]{.topic-badge}

### Remote sensing
What a satellite actually measures, the four resolutions, the vegetation
indices you will meet in every paper, and how to annotate a trajectory with
environmental covariates in space *and* time.

→ [Class 5](classes/class-05/slides.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Theme 4]{.topic-badge}

### Movement segmentation
An animal is not one thing all day. Behavioural states, change-point methods
and hidden Markov models: how to cut a trajectory into behaviourally
meaningful pieces, and how to avoid fooling yourself while doing it.

→ [Class 6](classes/class-06/slides.qmd)
:::

::: {.class-card}
[Theme 5]{.topic-badge}

### Resource and step selection functions
Use versus availability — the central idea of habitat selection. RSFs, then
step selection functions and integrated SSA, which fold movement and selection
into one model.

→ [Class 7](classes/class-07/slides.qmd) · [Class 8](classes/class-08/slides.qmd)
:::

## Before the first class

1. Install R, RStudio and the course packages — see **[Software setup](setup.qmd)**.
2. Download the **[datasets](data.qmd)**.
3. Bring a laptop. Every class has hands-on time.
